title: Site comparison preserves finite proper/open interchange
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. Use ordinary bounded-below derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ modules on small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For a qcqs morphism $u:U\to V$ write $a_u:C_Uu_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u_p^*C_V$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $b_u:C_VRu_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{p,*}C_U$ for its counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and for an open immersion $j$ write $e_j:C j_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{p,!}C$ for the canonical adjoint open-extension comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison, def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport]. Subscripts $e,p$ distinguish the two sites. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$, $r:U'\to U$ and $q:Z'\to Z$ form a Cartesian square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume all corners are Noetherian (each has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), $r,q$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and all arrows are qcqs. Let $\gamma^e:j_{e,!}Rr_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{e,*}j'_{e,!}$ be the proper-support-normalized map [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. On the pro-etale site let $\gamma^p:j_{p,!}Rr_{p,*}\to Rq_{p,*}j'_{p,!}$ be the canonical map whose $j_{p,!}\dashv j_p^*$ transpose is the inverse of the open base-change isomorphism $j_p^*Rq_{p,*}j'_{p,!}\cong Rr_{p,*}j_p'^*j'_{p,!}\cong Rr_{p,*}$, using the ordinary unit--counit exchange and the open-extension unit [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. For every $N\in D^+(U'_e,\Lambda)$ define
$$S_N=j_{p,!}(b_{r,N})\circ e_{j,Rr_{e,*}N},\qquad T_N=Rq_{p,*}(e_{j',N})\circ b_{q,j'_{e,!}N}.$$
Then
$$\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}\circ S_N=T_N\circ C_Z(\gamma^e_N),$$
and $\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}$ is an isomorphism.
